sectorSummary.overview: Growth remained positive across the reviewed platforms, but profit conversion varied sharply. Mature businesses showed operating leverage while quick commerce, home services and newer initiatives continued to absorb investment; PB Fintech faces material uncertainty over proposed insurance-distribution changes. Affle’s canceled call is excluded.

trends.text: Revenue or transaction measures grew year-on-year, although GMV, NOV, GOV and revenue have different definitions and should be compared within each company.
Customer acquisition, cross-selling and broader service offerings remain central to expanding platform monetization.

headwinds.text: Growth spending and newer initiatives continue to absorb cash or constrain near-term margin conversion.
Reported growth and profit comparisons require adjustments for accounting changes, acquisitions, seasonality or exceptional items.

opportunities.text: Nykaa’s Fashion profitability and owned brands, alongside CarTrade’s OLX monetization, offer opportunities to improve operating leverage.
Eternal and Swiggy see smaller cities, frequency and assortment as growth opportunities, with investment and profitability tradeoffs.
Payments platforms are expanding value-added services and financial-service distribution, while Urban Company is scaling new service use cases.

risks.text: PB Fintech expects lower distribution payouts under the proposed framework to reduce insurance-distribution revenue; mitigation and final rules remain uncertain.
Swiggy and Urban Company remain exposed to substantial investment losses in Instamart and InstaHelp respectively.
PhysicsWallah’s NEET/government-exam recovery and RateGain’s corporate-travel recovery remain incomplete.

insights.text: Eternal’s 76% adjusted-revenue growth includes inventory accounting; the like-for-like rate is 58%.
RateGain’s 152.6% reported revenue growth includes Sojern consolidation, versus 14% Q2 organic growth on a combined-business basis.
Paytm’s reported PAT comparison benefits from a prior-year exceptional loss; CarTrade’s PAT growth is depressed by a prior-year write-back and tax differences.
